findings.title: Coverage raw counts are not scoped to the product shape
findings.description: `raw_counts()` counts every `tick_trade` row in the supplied session intervals (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/status_reads.py:167-172`) without joining `unit_id` back to `tick_archive_unit`/`tick_request` or applying the shape predicate. `build_coverage()` filters the ledger by `shape_of(entry)` (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_coverage.py:107-109`) and then compares it to that unfiltered raw scan (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_coverage.py:113`). Because `Shape` is explicitly documented as “a product's request shape” (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/status_reads.py:30-44`) and `build_status()` is built for a sequence of universe entries (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_status_build.py:232-247`), a second product with overlapping sessions will produce false raw-count mismatches. The current one-product universe hides this, so the new integration tests cannot catch it. Scope the raw rows by dataset/symbols/stype-in/stored-tier shape while still detecting superseded or out-of-band rows, and add a multi-product regression test.

findings.title: Calendar outage errors are not normalized to the documented exit 4
findings.description: `calendar_sessions()` constructs `TradingCalendar` at `src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_status_build.py:67` outside the `try`, then catches only `psycopg.OperationalError`, `CalendarNotFoundError`, and `OutOfPopulatedRangeError` at lines 70-73. `TradingCalendar.__init__` uses `ConnectionPool(..., open=True)` (`src/manta_trading/data/base/trading_calendar.py#TradingCalendar.__init__`), and this project already treats `psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout` as a distinct pool failure (`src/manta_trading/cli/commands/data.py:406-416`; `test/integration/data/test_tick_ingest_plan.py:112-119`). A pool/constructor failure can therefore escape as `PoolTimeout`; `run_mapped()` maps only `TickDatabaseUnreachable` via its `storage` tuple and otherwise calls `exit_code_for()` (`src/manta_trading/cli/commands/tick_store_cmds.py:74-81`), which maps `TickCalendarError` and `psycopg.OperationalError` but not `PoolTimeout` (`src/manta_trading/cli/commands/tick_exit.py:38-58`). That contradicts `READ_EPILOG`’s promise of exit 4 for calendar unreachability (`src/manta_trading/cli/commands/tick_store_cmds.py:36-41`), and `test/integration/data/test_tick_status_cli.py:147-153` covers only an unreachable tick database. Wrap constructor/pool failures in the same calendar error boundary, include `PoolTimeout`, and add an unreachable-calendar CLI test.

findings.title: New database read paths lack the required load-tier coverage
findings.description: The changed commands add a network/DB read path that opens a calendar pool and can execute a large `count(*) FROM tick_trade` (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/status_reads.py:154-174`; `src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_coverage.py:93-114`). The Python rules require a load test for simulation, network, concurrency, or environment-layer paths, asserting latency, throughput, or resource bounds. The slice-225 load tier still contains only `test/load/test_225_tick_ingest_nfr.py`, whose header at lines 1-20 measures ingest time and event-loop gaps; no load test exercises `status`/`coverage` query latency, large session arrays, raw-row volume, or calendar-pool behavior. Add a gated load test with a realistic multi-session/row volume and a latency or resource bound for these read commands.

findings.title: Coverage can issue an unbounded `tick_trade` scan without a server statement timeout
findings.description: `tick_coverage` validates only that `--end` is after `--start` (`src/manta_trading/cli/commands/tick_store_cmds.py:216-221`), then `build_coverage()` derives all sessions in that arbitrary range and calls `raw_counts()` over `[min(open_ns), max(close_ns)]` (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_coverage.py:93-114`; `src/manta_trading/data/tick/status_reads.py:165-172`). `_read()` opens the connection through `connect_migrated()` and closes it but never sets `statement_timeout` (`src/manta_trading/cli/commands/tick_store_cmds.py:156-167`); `store_context.py#_connect` sets only `connect_timeout`. SQL rules require `statement_timeout` for long-running queries, and this coverage query can hold a backend for an unbounded range. Add a bounded server-side statement timeout with cancellation semantics, cap the date range/session count, and include EXPLAIN/latency evidence for the chosen bound.

structured_findings.summary: Coverage raw counts are not scoped to the product shape
Calendar outage errors are not normalized to the documented exit 4
New database read paths lack the required load-tier coverage
Coverage can issue an unbounded `tick_trade` scan without a server statement timeout
